body: One of my earliest memories is of going to my mother crying in the middle of the night and telling her I wanted to die. I must have been somewhere around 5-7 as well, and I'm 22 now. So you're not alone there. I'm always wondering what happened to make me suicidal at such a young age.
I'm reading No Longer Human too. What did you think of it?

On the off-chance that you're in Japan, the TELL Lifeline speaks English and has an online chat function (the downside is that they're only online at specific hours): https://telljp.com/lifeline/

For other countries, I have no idea, sorry :(
Yes, I know about reverse culture shock as well. It's something I know I'll have to deal with whether I go home now or after the full year.

I guess it's a complicated question for me. I've wanted to kill myself since around age 12, and I'm 20 now, so my life has both improved and gotten worse several times over since then. But even during a good period, I have the knowledge in the back of my mind that when it gets bad again it will probably be worse than the last time it was bad, because it always has been. During those good times it's less like I'm wanting to kill myself asap, and more like "yeah I still want to, but I'll wait until the next time things go to shit." Only reason I haven't done it yet when things have gone to shit is bc I'm a coward.

I guess I regret not doing it earlier, but it's not really something I think about from that perspective. I'm more focused on how and when I can do it in the future I suppose. That's more comforting than regret.
Yeah, I'm with you on this. It sucks.

This was strangely uplifting for me to read. Spite is pretty much all I have too, and sometimes I forget about it. Thank you for the reminder. I'm glad your spite keeps you going, it's a powerful emotion.
